title: System prompts, templates, and guardrails
task_statement: Apply system prompts, output contracts, and guardrails that keep instructions apart from data. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: System prompt with role, scope, and rules
components.first_principle: The system prompt sets the role, scope, and rules, while your code enforces access (Inference).

nodes.label: System prompt: role, scope, output rules

steps: Write the role, scope, and output rules in the top-level system field.
Tell Claude that tool results and documents are untrusted data.
Place untrusted content only in tool_result blocks, not in the system field.
Screen user input with a lightweight model such as Claude Haiku 5.5 before the main request.
Check the response in code before you show it or act on it.
Test each system prompt change with the evaluation set before release.
pros: A clear role focuses tone and behavior, even in a single sentence.
Untrusted content kept in tool results limits indirect prompt injection.
The system field keeps stable rules apart from user turns.
cons: A system prompt is guidance, so it does not enforce access on its own (Inference).
A long system prompt adds input tokens to every request.
An edit to the system content invalidates the system and message cache levels.
use_when: Every request needs the same role, scope, and output rules.
One assistant serves many users with one set of rules.
do_not_use_when: A rule must hold for every input. Enforce it in code instead (Inference).
The rule changes per request, for example with user identity or permissions.

constraints.choice: Keep stable instructions in one system block so the cache can hold them.
constraints.combination: On supported models, append a role system message to messages instead of an edit to the top-level system field.

constraints.choice: Test each system prompt change with the evaluation set before release.
constraints.combination: Roll back to the previous version when the evals drop.

constraints.choice: Keep system prompts in version control with a named version.
constraints.combination: Record the version with each logged response (Inference).

constraints.choice: Put tenant-specific access rules in code, not in the shared system prompt (Inference).

components.exam_tie: D2.2. Expect a scenario that separates guidance in the system prompt from enforcement in code. (Inference)
components.trap: A rule in the system prompt looks like access control, but it is guidance that code must enforce (Inference).
components.decision_rule: Put role and output rules in the system prompt. Put access rules in code.
components.exam_tip: When a scenario needs a hard limit, choose code enforcement over a longer system prompt.

components.name: Structured outputs as the output contract
components.first_principle: Structured outputs constrain the response to a JSON schema, so parsing errors leave the code path.

nodes.label: Valid JSON in the text block

steps: Define the output schema as JSON schema or as a type in your language.
Send the schema in the output_config format field with type json_schema.
Read the JSON from the text content block of the response.
Check the stop reason for refusal or max_tokens before you parse the text.
Validate business rules in code after you parse the fields.
pros: The response is valid JSON that matches the schema in most cases.
The docs state that schema violations need no retries in most cases.
Required fields and field types are guaranteed.
cons: The schema must use the supported JSON Schema subset.
An edit to output_config.format invalidates the prompt cache for that thread.
The first request with a new schema adds latency while the grammar compiles.
use_when: Downstream code parses the response into fields.
A pipeline needs a fixed JSON shape for every response.
do_not_use_when: A person reads free prose and no code parses the answer.
The schema uses a constraint that the JSON Schema limits reject.
The request needs citations, because citations with output_config.format return a 400 error.

constraints.choice: Keep the schema small to limit the added input tokens.
constraints.combination: Keep the format stable so the prompt cache survives.

constraints.choice: Use the schema instead of a retry loop for shape errors. Keep the schema stable, because a compiled grammar stays cached for 24 hours from last use.
constraints.combination: Add a business-rule check in code after parsing.

constraints.choice: Log the stop reason for each response, and count refusals.
constraints.combination: Alert on a rise in refusals after a prompt change (Inference).

constraints.choice: Version each schema with the application code.
Keep strict schemas within 20 strict tools, 24 optional parameters, and 16 union-type parameters per request.
constraints.combination: Split many strict tools across separate requests or subagents.

components.exam_tie: D2.2. Expect a scenario that asks for a fixed output shape for downstream code. (Inference)
components.trap: A prompt that asks for JSON only looks equal to a schema, but nothing constrains the text, so it can still break parsing.
components.decision_rule: Use structured outputs when code parses the answer. Use prose when a person reads it.
components.exam_tip: Check stop_reason for refusal or max_tokens before you parse, because both can return output that does not match the schema.
